title: Settings
intro: Adapt the agents and their payment guard to your business. Changes apply to the next conversation.
locked: Read-only: this server sets SETTINGS_LOCKED, so the public demo's keys and limits can't be changed.
lockedError: Settings are read-only on this server (SETTINGS_LOCKED).

language.title: Language
language.detail: The language of the menus, buttons and pages. It applies at once, in this browser only, without Save settings.
language.label: Interface language
language.failed: Could not change the language. Try again.

keyHint.env: Using {variable} from the server environment ({hint}). Leave blank to keep it.

business.detail: Who the agents work for and the refund policy they follow. The guard's AI judge checks every refund against this policy.
business.name: Business name
business.contactEmailsHint: The only addresses besides the customer's that replies may include.

limits.detail: Enforced by the guard whatever the AI decides: no prompt can raise them.
limits.autoRefundUpToHint: Smaller refunds run on their own.
limits.approvalUpToHint: Larger refunds wait on /guard; above this they are blocked.
limits.dailyCapHint: Total the agent may refund per day.

ai.detail: The model that runs the agents and the one that judges their calls. Any provider with an OpenAI-compatible API works: cloud, Chinese or running on your own machine.
ai.providerHint: {count} providers from the models.dev catalog, plus any OpenAI-compatible URL.
ai.agentModelHint: Answers the tickets and calls PayPal tools. Only models that can call tools are listed.
ai.judgeModelHint: Checks each refund against the policy.

paypal.detail: The agents reach PayPal through a REST app you create in the PayPal Developer Dashboard (developer.paypal.com, Apps & Credentials). Paste its sandbox client ID and secret here. Money in the sandbox is fictitious.
paypal.needCredentials: Enter the client ID and secret first.

notifications.detail: When the guard holds a call for a person, it tells every channel that is on. The message names the amount, the masked customer email and the rules, never the ticket's text.

webhook.title: Slack or Discord
webhook.detail: A message in a channel of your team chat, through an incoming webhook.
webhook.guide: How to get a Slack or Discord webhook
webhook.step1: Slack: on api.slack.com/apps, create an app from scratch in your workspace, open Incoming Webhooks, turn them on, click Add New Webhook to Workspace, pick the channel and copy the URL.
webhook.step2: Discord: in your server, open the channel's Edit Channel → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook, then Copy Webhook URL.
webhook.step3: Paste the URL above and save. The URL works as a password: anyone who has it can post to the channel.

email.title: Email
email.detail: An email to the contact emails under Business, through your own mail server (SMTP) when its server, login and password are set, otherwise through Resend.
email.fromHint: With SMTP, leave blank to send from the login. With Resend, a sender on a domain verified there, or onboarding@resend.dev to try it.
email.smtpPasswordForgets: Changing the server or login forgets it.
email.smtpGuide: How to set up email with your own mail (SMTP)
email.smtpStep1: Gmail: turn on 2-Step Verification for the account, then create an app password on myaccount.google.com/apppasswords. Use server smtp.gmail.com, port 587, your Gmail address as login and the 16-letter app password, without spaces. Your normal password does not work.
email.smtpStep2: Outlook or Microsoft 365: server smtp.office365.com, port 587, your address and password (an app password if the account uses two-step sign-in). Your administrator may need to allow SMTP for the mailbox.
email.smtpStep3: Your hosting's mail: the server, port and login are in your hosting panel's email settings, often mail.your-domain.com with your full address as login.
email.smtpStep4: Leave the from address blank: most mail servers only send from the account you log in with.
email.smtpStep5: The password only travels encrypted (TLS), and is only ever sent to the server and login it was saved with.
email.resendGuide: How to set up email with Resend
email.resendStep1: Sign up on resend.com (the free plan is enough), open API Keys, create a key with sending access and paste it above.
email.resendStep2: To try it: use onboarding@resend.dev as the from address and put your Resend account's email in Contact emails under Business. Resend's test sender only delivers to that address, and may land in spam.
email.resendStep3: For real: in Resend, open Domains, add your domain, add the DNS records it shows, and once it is verified use an address on it, like guard@your-domain.com.
email.resendStep4: Every contact email under Business gets the message.

telegram.title: Telegram
telegram.detail: A message from your own Telegram bot to a chat, a group or a channel.
telegram.chatIdHint: Message your bot, then open api.telegram.org/bot{token}/getUpdates and copy chat.id, or use @channelname.
telegram.step1: In Telegram, open @BotFather, send /newbot, choose a name and a username ending in bot, and paste the token it gives you (123456789:AA…) above.
telegram.step2: Open a chat with your new bot, press Start and send it any message. For a group, add the bot to the group and send a message there.
telegram.step3: In a browser, open {url}, with your token right after bot and no spaces or {brackets}. Copy the number in {chat} into Telegram chat id. A group's id starts with -100.
telegram.step4: If it shows {empty}, the bot has no message yet: send it one and reload.
telegram.step5: Set APP_URL on the server so the message links to the guard page; without it, Telegram shows /guard as a bot command.

save.scope: Saves every section, not only this one.
save.saved: Saved. The next ticket uses these settings.
